newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vranitzky says will try to reach Tirana Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Vranitzky says will try to reach Tirana Thursday.

text.p: Former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky, heading a European security body mission to Albania, said on Thursday he would try to reach Tirana later in the day despite reports that the airport there was closed.

Vranitzky, who first visited Tirana last week as head of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) mission, told a news conference he would probably travel by military plane to the Albanian capital.
Asked if he would travel by military plane, Vranitzky said: "It certainly will not be by civilian plane."

Vranitzky, who presented his report on behalf of the 54-member state OSCE on the current crisis in Albania on Wednesday, said he had not yet received word on whether his mission could hold talks with insurgents who have taken control of the Balkan state's southern region.

"We have had no direct reaction (regarding dialogue) from anyone on behalf of the insurgents, but the message from the prime minister (Bashkim Fino) is that we may be able to have contact and might be able to organise talks," Vranitzky said.

He said there were movements in the streets of Tirana but it was not nearly as bad as in other areas in the country. Shooting was clearly heard in the Albanian capital overnight after looters seized weapons from a military academy.
